stimulus:
Shards (unordered, unexplained):

- lacquer cracking into craquelure as the underlayer shrinks, so the failure pattern records the history of drying
- a ferry pilot reading standing waves off a river bar to infer a hidden sandbank
- sourdough starters that keep a community alive through periodic discarding
- the moiré that appears only when two regular grids are slightly misaligned
- bell founders tuning by shaving metal from the inside lip, not by adding any
- lichens: two kingdoms, one body, boundary negotiated daily
- a tide table kept by a village that has no moon calendar, only knots in rope
- the ear's cochlea performing a Fourier transform in a coiled, fluid-filled shell
- mycelial networks rerouting after a cut, with no central map
- negative space in a woodblock print doing half the carving work
- a locksmith who listens to what the lock refuses to do
- salt deliberately added to ice to make it colder, not warmer
- a pidgin becoming a creole when children inherit it
- kintsugi: the repair is the most valuable part
- an auction in which the losing bids are what carry the information
- fog nets harvesting water from air that never rains

Now, before answering the question below, pick three shards that seem least related to it. For each, extract the underlying mechanism in one sentence. Then use those mechanisms, not their imagery, to generate proposals that a standard literature review would not suggest. Reject your first three obvious ideas.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Craquelure-style chromatin fracture mapping after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Shard mechanism (lacquer craquelure): the pattern of failure records the history of the underlying shrinkage. After a transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or cytokine), later perturb the system with a stressor (AP-1 degron depletion, BAF inhibition) and map which enhancers lose accessibility (ATAC/CUT&Tag) and in what order. Compare the loss pattern between naive and previously stimulated cells to test whether the 'fracture' map encodes the history of earlier AP-1 exposure.

ideas.title: Losing-bid analysis: sites AP-1 binds but fails to open
ideas.description: Shard mechanism (auction losing bids carry information): the rejected options reveal the decision rules. Use time-resolved ChIP/CUT&RUN plus ATAC across repeated stimulations to catalog AP-1 motif sites that are bound transiently but never become accessible or never retain accessibility. Compare their sequence, nucleosome, and cofactor features with sites that are retained to define the rules for which AP-1 binding is converted into memory and which is not.

ideas.title: Moiré interference between two stimulus rhythms
ideas.description: Shard mechanism (moiré arises only when two regular grids are slightly misaligned): a slow beat pattern emerges from a small mismatch of periodic inputs. Deliver optogenetic or chemical AP-1 pulses at two slightly offset periods or in two pathways (e.g., JNK and ERK), then measure whether the residual enhancer accessibility and gene expression show a slow beat or phase-dependent memory. The aim is to test whether AP-1 integrates stimulus timing rather than just dose, and to distinguish dynamics-based memory from a simple ratchet.

ideas.title: Subtractive tuning: shave AP-1 dosage to find the memory-critical threshold
ideas.description: Shard mechanism (bell founders tune by removing metal, not adding): precision comes from graded subtraction of an existing structure. Instead of overexpression, use titratable degrons (dTAG/AID) or CRISPRi alleles of FOS/JUN family members and motif-site edits to remove AP-1 stepwise at defined times (during priming, during the delay, or during recall). Measure how recall amplitude and chromatin state change to separate AP-1's role in establishing, maintaining, and reading out memory, and identify any dose threshold.

ideas.title: Lineage-tracked inheritance test through division and passaging
ideas.description: Shard mechanism (sourdough starter keeps a community alive through periodic discarding): persistence through repeated partial removal indicates a self-propagating state. Prime cells with an AP-1 stimulus, then serially passage them with strong dilution, using barcoded lineages and single-cell multiome (RNA and ATAC) with live AP-1 reporters. Test whether the primed state persists, is heritable by clone, and re-establishes after dilution without the stimulus, and whether it needs continued AP-1 binding (acute degron versus none) to be passed on.
